content.title: South Carolina's defense stops UConn stars in Final Four victory
content.text: Updated April 3, 2026, 10:26 p.m. ETSouth Carolina is back in the national championship game.The Gamecocks had four players in double figures, led by Ta'Niya Latson's 16 points, and stymied UConn stars Sarah Strong and Azzi Fudd en route to a 62-48 victory in the Final Four on April 3 in Phoenix.South Carolina ended UConn's 54-game win streak.South Carolina (36-3) sprinted out of the halftime break with a 12-2 run to flip a UConn (38-1) two-point lead into a Gamecocks 8-point advantage.UConn responded with back-to-back-to-back 3-pointers before the end of the third quarter, but South Carolina never relinquished the lead.The Huskies cut the lead to 46-44 with 6:37 to play, but a Maddy McDaniel layup and a Agot Makeer 3-pointer provided the necessary cushion.UConn shot just 32% from the floor, with Strong (12 points on 4-of-16 shooting) and Fudd (eight points on 3-of-15 shooting) never getting comfortable against South Carolina’s physical and energetic defense.Another big margin of note: South Carolina out-rebounded UConn 47-32.The Gamecocks will play for the national championship on April 5 against the Texas-UCLA winner.Watch South Carolina women's basketball on Fubo South Carolina women's basketball vs UConn Final Four score South Carolina moves on with dominant second half to beat UConnAll the Geno Auriemma-related things aside, the Gamecocks dominate UConn in the second half to beat the Huskies 62-48 and move on to the national championship game.South Carolina outscored UConn 38-22 in the second half. The Huskies were just 2-of-18 from the floor on two-point shots in the second half. Dawn Staley, Geno Auriemma have heated postgame exchange Gamecocks continue to frustrate UConn's Sarah StrongSarah Strong knocks down an open 3 for her first points of the second half, but it was only a temporary reprieve for UConn's star forward.On the next possession, Strong pulled up and short-armed an open floater that could have cut the South Carolina lead to four with 3:23 left.It's been a fantastic defensive day for South Carolina through 37 minutes. Will the Gamecocks finish it off?South Carolina leads 55-47 with 2:11 left. South Carolina continuing to keep UConn at arm's lengthSouth Carolina's second made 3-pointer of the game: Agot Makeer, who extends the lead to 51-44 with 5:53 left. Makeer has a team-high 12 points.Four Gamecocks are in double figures. UConn's Sarah Strong is still scoreless in the second half, her last made basket on a layup with five minutes left in the second quarter. Geno Auriemma unhappy with officiatingGeno Auriemma ripped into the officiating during his between-quarters interview with ESPN.Among other things, Auriemma noted that all six fouls in the third quarter were called on UConn."Their coach rants and raves on the sideline, and calls the referees some names you don't want to hear," Auriemma said. "And now we got 6-0 (fouls called in the quarter) and I've got a kid (Sarah Strong) with a ripped jersey, and they go, 'I didn't see it.' C'mon, man. This is for the national championship."ESPN showed Strong ripping up her own jersey during the between-quarters timeout. South Carolina 44, UConn 39 after three quartersTessa Johnson has the final four points of the quarter to settle things down for South Carolina, who leads 44-39 with a quarter to go.The Gamecocks have been excellent defensively on Sarah Strong (8 points, 3-13 shooting) and Azzi Fudd (5 points, 2-9 shooting) through 30 minutes. UConn fighting back with three straight 3sKayleigh Heckel, Blanca Quinonez and Azzi Fudd hit 3-pointers on back-to-back-to-back possessions to cut South Carolina's lead to 40-39 with a minute to go in the third quarter.The Gamecocks had been pulling away before then. UConn had only made one 3-pointer before that stretch. South Carolina surging to start third quarterAgot Makeer hits from about 15 feet to extend South Carolina's lead to 36-28 midway through the third quarter. Timeout UConn.The Gamecocks open the quarter on a 12-1 run. UConn is 1-for-7 shooting in the third quarter and facing its largest deficit of the season. UConn leads South Carolina at halftimeUConn takes a 26-24 lead over South Carolina at halftime. The Gamecocks missed 10 of their last 11 shots in the first half.Tessa Johnson, Joyce Edwards and Ta'Niya Latson have six points each. UConn's Sarah Strong has 8 points on 3-of-10 shooting, while Azzi Fudd has two points from 1-of-6 shooting.The rebounding margin is lopsided: South Carolina 24, UConn 16. UConn retakes the lead on Azzi Fudd's first points of the gameAfter Joyce Edwards can't cash in on an offensive rebound from her own miss, UConn retakes the lead at 24-23 with a Azzi Fudd drive and score. Timeout South Carolina with 2:08 left before halftime. South Carolina 21, UConn 20 with 4:28 left in second quarter; Gamecocks limiting Azzi Fudd so farUConn cuts the Gamecocks' lead to one after a couple baskets prior to a media timeout. UConn's Azzi Fudd is scoreless, 0-for-3 so far through 14 minutes.South Carolina is shooting 36% but out-rebounding UConn 19-9. South Carolina leads 21-16 with bothersome defenseSouth Carolina is currently on a 11-1 run dating back to the final minute of the first quarter. UConn has missed its last five shots. Raven Johnson sits with two foulsRaven Johnson picks up two quick fouls on loose-ball plays and will sit with 8:28 left in the second quarter. Johnson has been the main defender against UConn's Sarah Strong. If Strong gets going here, Johnson may return to the floor soon. Agot Makeer 3-pointer ties the game after one quarterAgot Makeer drains a 3-pointer in the final seconds of the first quarter to tie the game at 15-all. Makeer has five points.Gamecocks have a 11-6 rebounding edge, including four offensive boards. UConn's Blanca Quinonez picks up two fouls in first quarterBlanca Quinonez picks up two fouls in a two-minute stint off the bench in the first quarter and will sit. She is an important depth player for UConn in the frontcourt. UConn leads 13-8 at first media timeout; South Carolina with 4 early turnoversQuick-paced start. UConn leads 13-8 with 3:27 left in the first quarter. Sarah Strong has five points on 2-of-5 shooting.South Carolina is trying to work through UConn's size early, and there's some good and bad. The Gamecocks have four turnovers leading to five Huskies points. Ta'Niya Latson and Tessa Johnson have four points apiece.Joyce Edwards has not attempted a shot yet. South Carolina vs UConn underway!South Carolina wins the tip, and it leads to a Ta'Niya Latson layup and an early lead. South Carolina vs UConn Final Four starting lineupsSouth Carolina: Raven Johnson, Ta'Niya Latson, Tessa Johnson, Joyce Edwards, Madina OkotUConn: Azzi Fudd, KK Arnold, Ashlynn Shade, Sarah Strong, Serah Williams Game time likely closer to 7:10 p.m.Given the game clock inside the arena in Phoenix and on the ESPN broadcast, expect tip off at around 7:10 p.m. South Carolina vs UConn women's basketball series historyUConn leads the series 11-5, including the national championship game win last spring. This year, the two programs did not play in the regular season for the first time since 2015. What time does South Carolina vs UConn start? Where: Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, ArizonaDate: April 3Time: 7 p.m. ET/ 4 p.m. PT Where to watch South Carolina vs UConn March Madness gameTV: ESPN which is available on Fubo, which offers a free trialSteaming: ESPN+How to watch online: Watch ESPN (here's how to stream it live) South Carolina vs UConn injury reportSouth CarolinaChloe Kitts: OutAdhel Tac: Out Dawn Staley vs Geno AuriemmaUConn coach Geno Auriemma is 10-5 against Staley. Before 2025, Staley was undefeated in national championship games and was the first coach to beat Auriemma in a title game.Staley, who is in her 18th season, didn't win against Auriemma until 2020. South Carolina won four straight from 2021-24.The Gamecocks are 5-11 in the series (one before Staley), which is tied 2-2 in neutral site games. South Carolina beat UConn in Columbia in 2024, part of its undefeated season that ended with a national championship win.Staley was 15 when Auriemma was in his first season with UConn in 1985-86.How many Final Four appearances does Geno Auriemma have?UConn just punched its ticket to a 25th Final Four, all under Auriemma.The Huskies have been to 17 of the last 18 Final Fours.How many Final Four appearances does Dawn Staley have?This will be Staley's eighth Final Four in the last 11 seasons and sixth straight with the Elite Eight win over TCU.Comparing South Carolina vs UConn statsUConn leads the nation in field goal percentage defense at 33.4%, South Carolina is sixth at 34.7%.UConn also leads the nation in field goal percentage, shooting 52%. South Carolina is third at 50.9%.Did Raven Johnson and Ta'Niya Latson play high school basketball together?Latson is a year younger than Johnson but the two played three seasons together for Westlake in Atlanta.Johnson signed with South Carolina as the No. 2 recruit in the Class of 2021 and Latson transferred to American Heritage High School in Florida for her senior year.Where Dawn Staley ranks among coaches with most NCAA women's basketball championshipsGeno Auriemma, UConn (12)Pat Summitt, Tennessee (8)Kim Mulkey, Baylor and LSU (4)Dawn Staley, South Carolina (3)Tara VanDerveer, Stanford (3)Linda Sharp, Southern Cal (2)Muffet McGraw, Notre Dame (2)Dawn Staley's March Madness record at South CarolinaStaley is 53-16 in the NCAA Tournament after winning four games in 2026.Dawn Staley contract, salaryOn Jan. 17, 2025, Staley's became the highest-paid college women’s basketball coach in the history of the sport.Staley's new contract took effect immediately and runs through 2029-30. She's receiving annual salary of $4 million with a $250,000 increase every season and a $500,000 signing bonus that makes the total value approximately $25.25 million.South Carolina women's basketball startersWith all players healthy, coach Dawn Staley's starting lineup is:PG- Raven JohnsonG- Ta'Niya LatsonG- Tessa JohnsonF- Joyce EdwardsC- Madina OkotSouth Carolina women's basketball 2025-26 rosterSenior Raven Johnson - Guard, No. 25Senior Ta'Niya Latson - Guard, No. 00Senior Chloe Kitts - Forward, No. 21Senior Maryam Dauda - Forward, No. 30Senior Madina Okot - Center, No. 11Junior Tessa Johnson - Guard, No. 5Sophomore Maddy McDaniel - Guard, No. 1Sophomore Joyce Edwards - Forward, No. 8Sophomore Adhel Tac - Forward, No. 15Freshman Ayla McDowell - Guard, No. 24Freshman Agot Makeer - Guard, No. 44Chloe Kitts injurySouth Carolina starting forward Chloe Kitts tore her ACL and will miss the entire 2025-26 season. Her father Jason confirmed via social media on Oct. 14 that she had a successful surgery and began the road to recovery.Kitts still travels with the team.She is returning next year, Staley confirmed on Feb. 25.Is Ashlyn Watkins playing for South Carolina this season?Ashlyn Watkins tore her ACL in Jan. 2025 and was set to return this season but won't.
